neighbours.label: the word 'job' as a person's employment position (holding, changing or leaving it)
fire: After the merger my uncle lost his job and moved back home.
Mina took a new job in Denver last winter.
The layoffs left him without a job for most of the year.
Many nurses are thinking about changing their job this year.
My cousin quit his job to open a bakery.
A better job across the country forced the family to relocate.
Graduates today rarely stay in one job for more than three years.
She applied for a job at the local library.
quiet: After the merger my uncle moved back home to help on the farm.
Mina took a long trip to Denver last winter.
The layoffs closed the factory for most of the year.
Many nurses are working night shifts at the clinic this year.
My cousin baked bread all morning at the new bakery.
Great job, the family said, when the boy finished the fence.
Graduates today rarely read a whole book in three years.
She applied a coat of paint at the local library.
